criteria.rationale: All four copies (repo and bootstrap template verify and inspect) start the preview in-process through Vite's preview() API in startPreview. Every exit path after the start closes it. verify's phaseRender and inspect's main both wrap the browser work in try/finally, which calls browser?.close() and then server.close(). criteria.rationale: the span audit's stated contradiction was confirmed by an independent check: The claim does not hold, because the first clause of the requirement is unmet. The requirement passes primitives only when "they type their props as the rendered element's props rather than an untyped bag". The quoted lines show that none of the primitives does this. Box, Label, Frame and Emphasis take NodeProps, a standalone kit interface with only id, x, y, w, h, className, style and children. SymbolChip takes SymbolChipProps and Arrow takes ArrowProps, both standalone interfaces. Appear and SceneLayer take inline object types. None of these types is built from the props of the rendered element (a motion.div, motion.span, motion.svg or div). Avoiding Record<string, unknown> does not make a type the rendered element's props. The guidance says typed primitives that "apply identity hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass". That describes primitives that accept and forward the element's caller props. These primitives accept none, so that pass case does not apply here. The quoted material shows clauses two and three are met: there is no spread of caller props onto the element, and the kit-only props do not reach the DOM. The material also shows the typing clause is not met, so the claimed pass is contradicted. | The auditor's point holds. The requirement sets out the complete pass condition, and its first clause says the primitives must "type their props as the rendered element's props rather than an untyped bag". That clause names a specific type: the props of the rendered element. Having some typed interface is not enough. The material shows that no public primitive meets it. Box, Label, Frame and Emphasis take NodeProps or an extension of it. NodeProps is a standalone kit interface with only id, x, y, w, h, className, style and children, and nothing in it derives from the props of motion.div or motion.span. ArrowProps is a standalone interface for a component that renders a motion.svg. Appear and SceneLayer take inline object types with only children, delay, className and style. The pass verdict relied on the guidance's list of failure examples, but that list illustrates failures and does not replace the requirement's positive condition. The guidance's pass case also describes primitives that apply identity hooks after caller props, which means primitives that accept and forward element props. These primitives forward none. Clauses two and three are met, since nothing is spread onto the element and kit-only props stay off the DOM. Clause one is not met, so the pass verdict is defeated.

Each scene wrapper is `position:absolute; inset:0`, so the outgoing scene is out of layout flow. The outgoing scene exits over EXIT_T (0.25s) while the incoming one fades in with no delay. result.rationale: The requirement says that when the skill scaffolds a presentation app, the scaffold must not define default presentation colors, fonts, button styles, borders or CSS theme tokens. The default scaffold breaks this. In scaffold.mjs, `starter` stays true unless `--no-starter` is passed (line 15), and it is passed to `scaffold(plan.appDir, { install, starter })` (line 30). In lib.mjs, `scaffold()` defaults `starter = true` (line 253) and calls `scaffoldIndex(appDir, report, starter)` whenever the index anchor is missing (lines 264-266). That covers every empty or unscaffolded target. `scaffoldIndex` then calls `createPresentation(appDir, 'getting-started', 'Getting Started', report)` when `withStarter` is true (lines 241-245). The body of `createPresentation` walks every file in `PRESENTATION_TEMPLATE_DIR` (which is `templates/presentation`, line 10). It writes each file, rendered, into `src/presentations/getting-started/` (lines 316-321). So the scaffolded app gets talk.css and Talk.tsx. talk.css defines theme tokens (`--ink`, `--muted`, `--gold`, `--line`, `--panel`, `--ok`), a `#0d0c0b` background and an Inter font stack (lines 3-15). It also defines button styles with padding, a 1px border and a 999px radius (lines 38-56), and bordered, rounded entity cards (lines 132-141). Talk.tsx imports './talk.css' and wraps the presentation in that class (lines 1-11), so the styling is active in the scaffolded output. SKILL.md 77-78 confirms that a fresh scaffold includes this `getting-started` presentation. Judges A and C ruled pass because the bootstrap package.json, vite.config.ts, src/index.css (`body { margin: 0 }`) and the kit are neutral, and A called talk.css presentation-owned and removable. Those facts are accurate, but they do not decide the requirement. The clause covers the scaffold's default output, and that output includes a starter whose stylesheet defines exactly the forbidden defaults. Saying the folder can be removed later (SKILL.md 77-78) does not stop the scaffold from writing it by default. SKILL.md's own neutrality claim (line 74) is prose, and the delivered helper behaves otherwise. C cites the integration test, but by Judge B's account it checks only the kit, package.json, vite.config.ts and index.css, so it never examines the generated starter stylesheet. Judge B's reason is borne out by the quoted lines and decides the clause.

votes.rationale: I traced every template the skill materializes against its documented destination and the kit's types. I found no import that resolves outside src, no unresolved CSS import, no missing required prop and no mismatched field name. The presentation templates are written to `<appDir>/src/presentations/<slug>/` by `createPresentation` in `lib.mjs`. From there, `Talk.tsx` imports `../../presentation-kit`, which is `src/presentation-kit/index.ts`. `steps/Scene.tsx` sits one level deeper and imports `../../../presentation-kit`, which resolves to the same place. `steps/Scene.tsx` imports `../entities`, `steps/index.ts` imports `./Scene`, and `Talk.tsx` imports `./steps`. All of those files exist in the template. `Talk.tsx` imports `./talk.css`, which is a template file with no `@import` of its own. The registry line that `registerInSource` writes is `import('./<slug>/Talk')` inside `src/presentations/index.ts`. That resolves to `src/presentations/<slug>/Talk`, and `Talk` has a default export, matching `PresentationEntry.load`. Props and field names match the kit types: - **`Presentation`:** `Talk.tsx` passes `steps`, `title` and `initialMode`. `PresentationProps` requires only `steps`. - **`Step`:** each entry in `steps/index.ts` supplies `id`, `era`, `title`, `caption`, `Scene`, `payload` and `groupKey`, which is every required field plus the optional `groupKey`. - **`Box` and `Label`:** the scene passes `id`, `x` and `y`, which `NodeProps` requires, plus optional `w`, `h` and `className`. - **`Arrow`:** the scene passes `id`, `from`, `to` and `className`. `ArrowProps` requires only `id`, `from` and `to`. - **`Appear` and `SceneLayer`:** both are given only `children`, which is all they require. - **`Scene`:** it is typed as `SceneProps<ScenePayload>`, matching `Step.Scene`. result.rationale: the span audit's stated contradiction was confirmed by an independent check: The claim does not hold, because the first clause of the requirement is unmet. The requirement passes primitives only when "they type their props as the rendered element's props rather than an untyped bag". The quoted lines show that none of the primitives does this. Box, Label, Frame and Emphasis take NodeProps, a standalone kit interface with only id, x, y, w, h, className, style and children. SymbolChip takes SymbolChipProps and Arrow takes ArrowProps, both standalone interfaces. Appear and SceneLayer take inline object types. None of these types is built from the props of the rendered element (a motion.div, motion.span, motion.svg or div). Avoiding Record<string, unknown> does not make a type the rendered element's props. The guidance says typed primitives that "apply identity hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass". That describes primitives that accept and forward the element's caller props. These primitives accept none, so that pass case does not apply here. The quoted material shows clauses two and three are met: there is no spread of caller props onto the element, and the kit-only props do not reach the DOM. The material also shows the typing clause is not met, so the claimed pass is contradicted. | The auditor's point holds. The requirement sets out the complete pass condition, and its first clause says the primitives must "type their props as the rendered element's props rather than an untyped bag". That clause names a specific type: the props of the rendered element. Having some typed interface is not enough. The material shows that no public primitive meets it. Box, Label, Frame and Emphasis take NodeProps or an extension of it. NodeProps is a standalone kit interface with only id, x, y, w, h, className, style and children, and nothing in it derives from the props of motion.div or motion.span. ArrowProps is a standalone interface for a component that renders a motion.svg. Appear and SceneLayer take inline object types with only children, delay, className and style. The pass verdict relied on the guidance's list of failure examples, but that list illustrates failures and does not replace the requirement's positive condition. The guidance's pass case also describes primitives that apply identity hooks after caller props, which means primitives that accept and forward element props. These primitives forward none. Clauses two and three are met, since nothing is spread onto the element and kit-only props stay off the DOM. Clause one is not met, so the pass verdict is defeated.

result.rationale: The criterion is met. No delivered browser-driving test sleeps for a fixed time. Which tests touch a browser: vitest.integration.config.ts:8 limits browser and filesystem tests to tests/integration/**/*.test.ts and tests/e2e/**/*.test.ts. Per the file list, those are exactly three files: tests/e2e/verify.test.ts, tests/integration/inspect.test.ts and tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts. All three are quoted in full. Every other test runs under vitest.config.ts with environment 'jsdom' (line 7), so none of them drives a browser. What the browser tests do: none of the three files opens a Playwright page or calls waitForTimeout, a sleep, or a timed setTimeout. Each one spawns the project scripts through runAsync or run. runAsync resolves only on the child's 'close' event (tests/helpers.ts:60), and the tests assert only after that, on exit status, output and report.json. The setTimeout at verify.test.ts:96 is a 0 ms delay inside text injected into the fixture to throw an uncaught error. It is a fault-injection payload, not a wait in the test. Where the scripts step the deck, they wait on observable state. After each ArrowRight, verify.mjs:71-76 calls waitForStepIndex. preview.mjs:58-63 implements that as page.waitForFunction, polling until data-step-index equals the target, with a timeout. votes.rationale: A transition that fails to advance is detected and tested. However, the step count is read as Number(await page.getAttribute(..., 'data-step-count')). A missing attribute gives Number(null) === 0, and a non-numeric one gives NaN. In both cases `i < count` is false, so no steps are stepped through and the run still ends in PASS. The only guard is `outline && count !== outline.length`, which applies to the reference slug alone. Every other registered presentation (outline is null) can therefore pass with zero steps checked. The initial step index is also never checked.

votes.rationale: I traced every template the skill materializes against its documented destination and the kit's types. I found no import that resolves outside src, no unresolved CSS import, no missing required prop and no mismatched field name. The presentation templates are written to `<appDir>/src/presentations/<slug>/` by `createPresentation` in `lib.mjs`. From there, `Talk.tsx` imports `../../presentation-kit`, which is `src/presentation-kit/index.ts`. `steps/Scene.tsx` sits one level deeper and imports `../../../presentation-kit`, which resolves to the same place. `steps/Scene.tsx` imports `../entities`, `steps/index.ts` imports `./Scene`, and `Talk.tsx` imports `./steps`. All of those files exist in the template. `Talk.tsx` imports `./talk.css`, which is a template file with no `@import` of its own. The registry line that `registerInSource` writes is `import('./<slug>/Talk')` inside `src/presentations/index.ts`. That resolves to `src/presentations/<slug>/Talk`, and `Talk` has a default export, matching `PresentationEntry.load`. Props and field names match the kit types: - **`Presentation`:** `Talk.tsx` passes `steps`, `title` and `initialMode`. `PresentationProps` requires only `steps`. - **`Step`:** each entry in `steps/index.ts` supplies `id`, `era`, `title`, `caption`, `Scene`, `payload` and `groupKey`, which is every required field plus the optional `groupKey`. - **`Box` and `Label`:** the scene passes `id`, `x` and `y`, which `NodeProps` requires, plus optional `w`, `h` and `className`. - **`Arrow`:** the scene passes `id`, `from`, `to` and `className`. `ArrowProps` requires only `id`, `from` and `to`. - **`Appear` and `SceneLayer`:** both are given only `children`, which is all they require. - **`Scene`:** it is typed as `SceneProps<ScenePayload>`, matching `Step.Scene`. Unused imports are not a problem under `noUnusedLocals`, because every import in the templates is used. The inspect template is `scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs`, and the scaffold copies the whole `scripts/` tree, including `lib/`. Its relative imports are `./lib/diagnostics.mjs`, `./lib/preview.mjs`, `./lib/settle.mjs` and `./lib/snapshot.mjs`. All four exist in the bootstrap template. The named imports match the actual exports: - **`diagnostics.mjs`:** `ATTRIBUTION_HINT`, `findAttributionIssues`, `findClippedChrome`, `findIndistinctActive`, `findOverlaps`, `findSmallText` and `SMALL_TEXT_MIN_PX`. - **`preview.mjs`:** `launchBrowser`, `sleep`, `startPreview` and `waitForStepIndex`. - **`settle.mjs`:** `settleThenCapture`. - **`snapshot.mjs`:** `collectSnapshot`. `diagnostics.mjs` imports nothing, and `MIN_RENDERED_TEXT_PX` is defined inside it. `preview.mjs` imports `playwright` and `vite`, and both are in the bootstrap `package.json` devDependencies. The requirement passes primitives only when "they type their props as the rendered element's props rather than an untyped bag". The quoted lines show that none of the primitives does this. Box, Label, Frame and Emphasis take NodeProps, a standalone kit interface with only id, x, y, w, h, className, style and children. SymbolChip takes SymbolChipProps and Arrow takes ArrowProps, both standalone interfaces. Appear and SceneLayer take inline object types. None of these types is built from the props of the rendered element (a motion.div, motion.span, motion.svg or div). Avoiding Record<string, unknown> does not make a type the rendered element's props. The guidance says typed primitives that "apply identity hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass". That describes primitives that accept and forward the element's caller props. These primitives accept none, so that pass case does not apply here. The quoted material shows clauses two and three are met: there is no spread of caller props onto the element, and the kit-only props do not reach the DOM. The material also shows the typing clause is not met, so the claimed pass is contradicted.

contradiction_checks.rationale: The auditor's point holds. The requirement sets out the complete pass condition, and its first clause says the primitives must "type their props as the rendered element's props rather than an untyped bag". That clause names a specific type: the props of the rendered element. Having some typed interface is not enough. The material shows that no public primitive meets it. Box, Label, Frame and Emphasis take NodeProps or an extension of it. NodeProps is a standalone kit interface with only id, x, y, w, h, className, style and children, and nothing in it derives from the props of motion.div or motion.span. ArrowProps is a standalone interface for a component that renders a motion.svg. Appear and SceneLayer take inline object types with only children, delay, className and style. The pass verdict relied on the guidance's list of failure examples, but that list illustrates failures and does not replace the requirement's positive condition. The guidance's pass case also describes primitives that apply identity hooks after caller props, which means primitives that accept and forward element props. These primitives forward none. Clauses two and three are met, since nothing is spread onto the element and kit-only props stay off the DOM. Clause one is not met, so the pass verdict is defeated.

result.rationale: The criterion is met. No delivered browser-driving test sleeps for a fixed time. Which tests touch a browser: vitest.integration.config.ts:8 limits browser and filesystem tests to tests/integration/**/*.test.ts and tests/e2e/**/*.test.ts. Per the file list, those are exactly three files: tests/e2e/verify.test.ts, tests/integration/inspect.test.ts and tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts. All three are quoted in full. Every other test runs under vitest.config.ts with environment 'jsdom' (line 7), so none of them drives a browser. What the browser tests do: none of the three files opens a Playwright page or calls waitForTimeout, a sleep, or a timed setTimeout. Each one spawns the project scripts through runAsync or run. runAsync resolves only on the child's 'close' event (tests/helpers.ts:60), and the tests assert only after that, on exit status, output and report.json. The setTimeout at verify.test.ts:96 is a 0 ms delay inside text injected into the fixture to throw an uncaught error. It is a fault-injection payload, not a wait in the test. Where the scripts step the deck, they wait on observable state. After each ArrowRight, verify.mjs:71-76 calls waitForStepIndex. preview.mjs:58-63 implements that as page.waitForFunction, polling until data-step-index equals the target, with a timeout. The scripts read titles and captions only after that. Judge C's fail does not decide the criterion. The sleep(SETTLE_MS) at verify.mjs:78 is in the verification script, not in a test. It runs after the waitForStepIndex poll has already confirmed the step, so it does not replace a state wait. The guidance also lists longer fixed settle delays as validator noise. INT-002's SETTLE_MS of 1300 (inspect.test.ts:6, 110, 138) is a CLI argument passed to the inspect tool, and the test then asserts on the recorded capturedAfterMs. The test itself never sleeps. Judges A and B (pass) are borne out. The only fixed timer in the test tree is at nodes.test.tsx:93. It is in a jsdom component test, not a browser test, and the assertion that waits for the settled opacity uses polling waitFor (line 96).

engineering-quality.rationale: The fail verdict rests only on the first clause: it says the props are a custom NodeProps interface rather than the rendered element's props. The requirement states that clause as a contrast with "an untyped bag such as Record<string, unknown>". The review guidance fails a primitive only when it uses such an untyped bag, spreads caller props after its identity hooks, or forwards a kit-only prop to the DOM. The guidance also says "Typed primitives that apply identity hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass." The material shows explicitly typed interfaces (NodeProps, BoxProps, SymbolChipProps, ArrowProps, and inline typed props for Appear and SceneLayer), not an untyped bag. No primitive spreads caller props onto the motion or DOM element. The layoutId, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id are set as fixed values, so a caller cannot override them. Kit-only props stay off the DOM: Icon is rendered as a child, variant maps to data-presentation-variant, label maps to aria-label/role, x/y/w/h feed boxStyle, and from/to/bend/both and delay are consumed internally. All three clauses, read with the guidance, are met, so the fail is defeated.
evidence: src/presentation-kit/nodes/shared.ts defines `export interface NodeProps { id: string; x: number; y: number; w?: number; h?: number; className?: string; style?: CSSProperties; children?: ReactNode }`…

src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx destructures `{ id, Icon, variant, className, children, ...rest }` and passes `rest` only to `boxStyle({ id, ...rest })`. The motion.div sets layoutId={id}, data-pr…
Label.tsx, Frame.tsx and Emphasis.tsx follow the same pattern: they spread no caller props and set the hooks as fixed values.
SymbolChip.tsx uses `label` only for `aria-label={label}` and `role`. Icon is rendered as a child element.
Arrow.tsx consumes from/to/bend/both internally to build the path. Its motion.svg sets layoutId={id} and data-presentation-id={id} as fixed values; only `style` is spread inside the style object.
Appear.tsx and SceneLayer.tsx use inline typed prop objects and set data-presentation-appear and data-presentation-layer as fixed values, with no caller spread.

engineering-quality.rationale: The criterion fails a helper that runs its diagnostics on only one step, such as only the final step, instead of on every captured step. It also fails captures that crop out the presentation's chrome. Neither happens here. In both inspect copies, the overlap, indistinct-active, clipped-chrome and small-text diagnostics all run inside every loop iteration, on a fresh snapshot of the whole page taken after that step's screenshot. The screenshots are full-viewport and uncropped. The snapshot collects controls, the table of contents, progress items, attribution, header and footer from the whole document. The auditor's point is true but narrow: the attribution check is guarded by i === 0, so only step 1 checks the attribution link, which belongs to the presentation as a whole. That does not mean the diagnostics run on a single step. The guidance also says whether individual warnings fire is scored by the visual-helper criteria, not here. So the cited fact does not defeat the pass.
